title: Edna and Mildred Dixon, Duke's wives and partners
summary: Bigard knew little of Edna, whom he calls evil, and likes Mildred Dixon, who danced at the Cotton Club with Henry Wesson; he will not name who caused Edna to slit Duke's face.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Did Edna go back to Washington somewhere along the --
Oh, she used to go back and forth all the time.
Was she in Washington when you took up with Mildred Dixon or was she still in New York?
She was in New York. She was a -- I never knew much about Edna.
(Unintelligible)
No, she was an evil -- But Mildred is a cute little gal. She's cute. She was real nice. She used
to dance with a fellow called Henry --
I think -- (Inaudible) it ought to be in Vianen's book,
Uh-huh.
But -- yeah, well, they were partners anyway and she used to dance with him. I'll think of that -- it had come along from the Cotton Club show.
Uh-huh.
Ah --
Do you know what it was that Duke did that got him cut?

No. I don't know what happened. But, see, that was way after -- She cut him way before I knew him and I didn't know what -- But then I know she used to -- I heard. I don't like to mention names, I mean, because it wouldn't be nice. So I'll be discreet.
Well, you can --

But he was quite a figure in the music world. That's all I'll say, and a real gentleman. That's about it. And I imagine Duke heard about it and got after her and they had a big argument and she waited till he went to sleep and slit him on his face with a razor blade.
I think the dancer that Mildred did some dances with was Henry Wesson.
Henry Wesson? that's it.
That's what it says in Barry Vianen's book.
(Inaudible)
What a wonderful guy.
